newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie rallies but far short of recovery.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie rallies but far short of recovery.

text.p: *AUD enjoyed first bounce for a while overnight as selling out of Zurich was soaked up by U.S. and other Swiss banks
*Squeeze caught market very short and speculators now hunting stops atop $0.7520, but resistance stiff there
*Break $0.7535 would argue for pause in downtrend but charts still bearish and recovery unlikely while rate risk looms
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar was struggling to keep the momentum going at US$0.7509/14 having firmed from US$0.7480/85 late here Tuesday.

Analysts cautioned a break of US$0.7535 was needed to suggest this was anything more than a blip in a downtrend and the currency would have to recover all the way past major resistance at US$0.7630/7680 to reverse the trend.

While US$0.7535 capped, they looked for a re-test of US$0.7475/80 and eventually supports at US$0.7450 and US$0.7420. Beyond there analysts saw a risk of a return to the 1996 trough of 73 cents on a one to month horizon.

On the crosses the currency inched up to 85.01/11 yen from 84.64/74 but remained hostage to the fortunes of US$/yen which was waiting anxiously for Japanese trade data at 9.50 am our time. The current account surplus is expected to have soared in May to around 592 billion against 229 billion a year ago.
Some forecasts went even higher and dealers feared such an outcome would inflame US/Japanese trade tensions to the detriment of both dollars.
Inflation data from the U.S. overnight also had implications for the A$ since the benign 0.1 percent rise in CPI provided another reason for the Federal Reserve not to hike in July.
A Fed tightening would further boost the US$'s differential advantage over the A$, so the diminising prospect of a hike would normally be positive for the local currency.

However, it was not so clear cut in this case since dealers suspected the less the chance of a U.S. move the more chance there was of the Reserve Bank easing here. Many reckoned that if the Fed did stand pat at its next meeting on July 1-2 the RBA would see it as a window of opportunity to cut rates.
A similar argument weighing on would-be bulls was that if the dollar itself managed a sustained rally that too would provide room for an easing. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
